svg.title: Extending the Agent Mesh: Ports and Adapters
svg.desc: Read left to right. On the left, the core: the domain and the message path, plain Rust, which depends only on its ports. In the middle, seven of its ports, the Rust traits it defines: Proposer, Bus, Record (RecordWriter and RecordReader), Gate, TelemetryWriter, SecretReader and ActionGateway; the core calls each. On the right, the adapter that implements each port and ships with the Agent Mesh: a model provider, which may instead be a script or a person; NATS JetStream for the bus and for the record; rule rows for the Gate; Prometheus for telemetry; Kubernetes Secrets for secrets; and the agent MCP gateway, a sidecar container, for actions. Above the core, an Agent definition, a Markdown file the install supplies, is loaded on reload. Below the ports, an MCP connection, a Markdown file the install supplies, is read by the gateway. Below the gateway, the two kinds of MCP server it calls over MCP: a vendor's, outside the mesh, and the install's own. The captions say that each adapter implements one port and passes the conformance kit; that an Agent and a connection are Markdown files read at a reload; that swapping a part is a Rust crate of the install's own built into a release; and that an MCP server of the install's own, in any language, is reached like a vendor's.
